## Body

# Correctness verdict: BLOCK, source-based

PR #194 at `f4d0e459579f4decb7a6023e204d575898e80e21`, answering `01a1bcca-010c-79d1-bb7f-8df571bf58fb`. The existing 29-kind admission guards work, but the required inventory/build guarantee and one shipped producer remain incomplete.

## Findings

**F001: adding an enum kind can silently omit its reservation.** `NoticeKind` and `NoticeKind::ALL` are independently maintained (`crates/core/src/notice_id.rs:21-124`). Reservation, the core's every-kind test and the scanner's listed-prefix/minted-kind checks enumerate only ALL (`notice_id.rs:162-188`; `crates/daemon/tests/notice_ids.rs:113-157`). The other controls check caller-ID shapes and bare-literal construction, not enum-to-table membership.

Adding a new enum variant, its exhaustive `prefix` match arm and a typed `NoticeKind::New.id(...)` producer, but forgetting ALL, leaves the new prefix unreserved without failing these tests. The scanner sees no bare-literal mint, the core tests never visit the variant, and the inventory loop never checks it. M5 exercises a different failure: replacing a listed kind with a bare-literal mint. It does not prove enum-to-ALL exhaustiveness.

**Fix:** make enum, ALL and prefixes one source, or add an independently exhaustive membership check. Add the new-variant/prefix/producer-without-ALL mutant and show the gate fails. PM confirmed that a new kind failing the build is required, not an optional sensor improvement.

**F002: the shipped background sidecar still emits predictable, unreserved daemon IDs.** `BgWorker` uses `bg-{id}-cancelled` and `bg-{id}-terminal` (`crates/sidecars/src/background.rs:313-323,423-437`). Both calls use BG_ACTOR and `enqueue_turn`, which writes a delivery row with that exact ID as its dedupe key and local origin (`sidecars/src/common.rs:186-216`).

This is reachable code, not an unused fixture: `Sidecars::new/start` constructs and starts BgWorker (`sidecars/src/runtime.rs:38,71`); daemon boot starts those sidecars (`crates/daemon/src/lib.rs:1086-1105,1135`). The authenticated `/v1/sidecar` accepts Bg start/cancel commands. Their job name is caller-known, and an ordinary sender can first occupy the corresponding delivery ID because none of the 29 reserved prefixes matches `bg-`. The completion/cancellation notice then loses the intended dedupe slot.

The scanner does read this file but misses these constructors: the format strings are arguments to `enqueue_turn`, not assignments to `msg_id`/`notice_id` or the first expression of an `_id` helper (`notice_ids.rs:80-109`). Therefore the currently green scanner is not proof of complete producer coverage.

**Fix:** reserve the background-sidecar namespace and migrate both producers through the typed mint, preserving existing `bg-` ID bytes. Extend the scanner/control for this constructor shape, and add a regression rejecting a caller's pre-reservation followed by the actual background-sidecar completion/cancellation notice landing once.

Both findings are source traces; no reviewer-executed mutation or runtime reproduction is claimed.

## Verified portions

- `/v1/send` rejects a reserved caller ID before the local/peer split, reply effects, role routing, FYI holding, control admission or ordinary delivery (`http/mod.rs:1952-1958`). The Telegram sidecar rejects both send/document IDs before enqueue or document staging (`:4635-4647`).
- Other routes do not accept an arbitrary caller-supplied delivery ID: shim send/control/attachments mint theirs internally; governance dispatch mints its ID; inbox hold/release use queued-row identity and do not create a caller-chosen delivery. Bg/chore command queue IDs are internally generated. F002 concerns their missing notice namespace, not another direct external message-ID field.
- Read all producer rewrites: the 28 retained prefixes and their suffix formatting are unchanged. Withdrawal deliberately changes `<id>.withdrawn` to `request-withdrawn-<id>`. The PR acknowledges that a previously held withdrawal retried across an upgrade can duplicate once under the new key. The claimed absence of live old rows is author-provided evidence, not a reviewer store probe.
- The 29-kind test rejects seven caller forms per kind. It then proves one representative internal FYI is held once and one representative internal queue notice is queued once with the daemon's body. This is admission/dedupe proof, not 29 individual emitter executions or completed model delivery.
